title: Opposition plans to seek a discussion on the embezzlement of donations at the Ayodhya Ram temple
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
• July 30, 2026 13:00
    Rajya Sabha adjouned till 2 p.m.
  • rajya sabha
    July 30, 2026 13:00
    Shobha Karandlaje, MoS for Labour and Employment, replies on protection for women workers under Labour Codes

    Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for Labour and Employment, said that the government has increased paid maternity leave to 26 weeks for women and introduced provisions for work-from-home options.

    She added that the Labour Codes prohibit gender discrimination, guarantee equal wages for equal work, and provide a grievance redressal mechanism for women workers. Furthermore, she emphasised that the Codes protect women’s right to work in any industry.

  • July 30, 2026 12:31
    Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav answers to questions raised on Biodiversity Finance
  • July 30, 2026 12:20
    Government recognised the gig workers in the Labour Code: Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of Labour and Employment

    Mansukh Mandaviya said in the Rajya Sabha during the Question Hour, that the government has recognised gig workers in the Labour Codes. “Gig workers can register themselves through the e-Shram portal. We have a separate model for social security for gig workers in the Labour Codes, where we have also kept some flexibility,” he replied when asked, why the government abstained from implementing the social security framework prescribed by the International Labour Organization.

  • rajya sabha
    July 30, 2026 11:59
    Pramod Boro, UPP(L) MP from Assam, speaks on implementation of Bodo Accord

    Pramod Boro, UPP(L) MP from Assam, paid tributes to the victims of the Assam floods in the House. Speaking on the implementation of the Bodo Accord and peace in the north-east, he said, “We look forward to a lasting peace in the region”

  • July 30, 2026 11:50
    Jogen Mohan, MP from Assam, draws attention to Assam flood; requests for additional help from central govt.

    Drawing attention to the Assam floods, MP Jogen Mohan said that long-term flood control measures are needed to mitigate flooding in the State.

  • July 30, 2026 11:44
    Surendra Singh Nagar demands for 'One nation One digital Metro card' during Zero Hour

    Surendra Singh Nagar speaks on the need for ‘One Nation One Digital Metro Card’ during Zero Hour.

  • rajya sabha
    July 30, 2026 11:33
    Opposition is disrupting the House: Leader of the House, J.P. Nadda

    Leader of the House, J.P. Nadda said that Opposition parties are disrupting the House during the Zero Hour. He said that, “Opposition has no issues; Govt. is ready to discuss on anything.”

  • rajya sabha
    July 30, 2026 11:13
    Heavy sloganeering in RS by Opposition

    Opposition parties started sloganeering in Rajya Sabha, demanding answers from Home Minister Amit Shah on police violence on students. 

  • lok sabha
    July 30, 2026 11:05
    Lok Sabha adjourned till 2 p.m. amid Opposition protest

    Lok Sabha adjourned till 2 p.m. soon after commencing on Thursday (July 30, 2026)

  • lok sabha
    July 30, 2026 11:03
    Lok Sabha proceedings begins

    Lok Sabha proceedings begins. LS Speaker congratulates winners at Commonwealth Games.

  • July 30, 2026 10:51
    Opposition leaders hold protest inside Parliament premises

    Opposition leaders hold protest inside Parliament premises over police action during Jantar Mantar protest.- PTI

  • July 30, 2026 10:37
    Congress MP Manish Tewari submits an Adjournment Motion in Lok Sabha to discuss "the contours of a new Anti-Defection Law"

    Congress MP Manish Tewari submitted on Thursday (July 30) an Adjournment Motion in Lok Sabha to discuss “the contours of a new Anti-Defection Law that proscribes Mass Political Defections driven by opportunism and bereft of any genuine ideological or policy differences while simultaneously providing space for honest and critical dissent both inside and outside Parliament and the legislatures.”

  • lok sabha
    July 30, 2026 10:16
    Lok Sabha to receive two Standing Committee on External Affairs reports

    According to the List of Business, the Lok Sabha will also receive two reports of the Standing Committee on External Affairs, including reports on “India’s Role and Presence in the Arctic and Antarctic Regions” and the action taken by the government on recommendations relating to the future of India-Bangladesh relations.

  • rajya sabha
    July 30, 2026 10:16
    Congress MP submits notice seeking urgent discussion on Ram Temple donation 'scam'

    Congress Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Singh Surjewala on Thursday (July 20, 2026) submitted a formal notice under Rule 267, seeking the suspension of listed business to discuss alleged financial irregularities, embezzlement, and donation looting linked to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.

    In his notice addressed to the Rajya Sabha Secretary-General, Mr. Surjewala urged the Chair to set aside all pre-scheduled legislative work for an urgent, high-priority debate to establish government accountability.

    The notice highlights that millions of devotees across the globe contributed thousands of crores of rupees through collective, individual, and secret donations out of deep religious faith.

    “This is because the matter of theft of donations, looting of offerings, and embezzlement in the Shri Ram Temple is not only a dacoity on the faith of millions of devotees, but it is also a direct case of loot, embezzlement, and corruption committed by the members and associated employees of the Shri Ram Temple Trust constituted under the orders of the Hon’ble Supreme Court,” the notice read.

    ANI

  • lok sabha
    July 30, 2026 10:16
    Congress MP moves Adjournment Motion to discuss new Anti-Defection Law

    Congress MP Manish Tewari on Thursday (July 30, 2026) submitted an Adjournment Motion Notice in the Lok Sabha, seeking a discussion on the contours of a new Anti-Defection Law.

    In his notice, Mr. Tewari called for a legal framework that can prevent “mass political defections driven by opportunism” and those not based on genuine ideological or policy differences.

    The Congress leader stressed the need for a balance between curbing political defections and protecting the right to “honest and critical dissent” among elected representatives inside and outside Parliament and state legislatures. He has urged the House to take up the matter for a detailed discussion, highlighting the need to revisit the existing anti-defection provisions and strengthen democratic accountability.

    ANI

  • July 30, 2026 10:16
    Opposition plans to raise Ram Temple donation scam in Parliament

    An emerging consensus is taking shape within the INDIA bloc that the Opposition should continue pursuing the Ram Temple embezzlement case in Parliament. The Samajwadi Party (SP), which has been raising the matter during meetings of Opposition parties, on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) staged a protest in the Parliament House complex.

    According to senior Opposition leaders, it was decided that the issue will be taken up in the Lok Sabha on Thursday (July 30 , 2026) and in the Rajya Sabha after the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, is cleared. The Opposition wants to seek a discussion on the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ayodhya Ram temple.

    Opposition plans to address the Ram Temple donation scam in Parliament, with the Samajwadi Party leading the charge.

title: Bankipur byelection: Polling begins as all eyes on contest between Prashant Kishor and BJP’s Neeraj Kumar Sinha
author: PTI
content_html:
Around 4.6% of 3.8 lakh voters exercised their franchise in the first two hours of polling in the Bankipur Assembly by-election in Bihar on Thursday (July 30, 2026), an official said.

The voting began at 7 a.m. in 422 polling stations and will continue till 6 p.m.

“The polling has so far been peaceful. The voter turnout till 9 a.m. was 4.61%,” the official said.

Altogether 26 candidates, including Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor, are in the fray.

Mr. Kishor, 49, a former poll strategist who launched the Jan Suraaj Party a few years ago, is contesting his first election, while the BJP, which has never lost the seat since 1995 when it was known as Patna West, has fielded low-key youth wing leader Neeraj Kumar Sinha.

Mr. Kishor’s entry has intensified the contest in a constituency where the BJP has won by huge margins over the years.

Mr. Nabin, who gave up the seat in April upon election to the Rajya Sabha, had won the Assembly segment for the fifth consecutive time in November last year, defeating nearest rival Rekha Gupta, the RJD candidate fielded by her party again this time, by over 50,000 votes.

Prominent politicians among those who voted till 9 a.m. include senior BJP leader C.P. Thakur, his son and Nawada MP Vivek Thakur and State Minister Ramkripal Yadav.

Mr. Nabin appealed to electors to come out in large numbers and cast their votes to strengthen the resolve of a developed India.

“I appeal to all the voters of the Bankipur (Bihar), Manjalpur (Gujarat) and Datia (Madhya Pradesh) assembly constituencies, especially the youth and women, to come out in large numbers to cast their votes and make their invaluable contribution toward strengthening the resolve of a Vikashit Bharat,” he wrote in his X post.

BJP’s Bihar unit president Sanjay Saraogi also urged people to exercise their franchise early in the day for the development of Bankipur.

Mr. Kishor on Thursday accused the Bihar Police of having picked up many of his supporters, allegedly at the behest of the ruling BJP, which he said “fears losing the bypoll” in the Bankipur seat.

title: CJP’s Dipke warns Govt. against 'harassing' students; seeks action over pellet gun use
author: PTI
content_html:
Asserting that student protesters are "not terrorists," Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) demanded action against officials who ordered pellet gun firing at Jantar Mantar on July 20, warning that the youth will "change the government" if police harassment continues.

Returning home after a month-long protest in New Delhi that led to the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak, Mr. Dipke claimed police across multiple States are visiting student activists' homes and threatening them with arrest.

"The government should behave well now. The blood of students was spilled on the streets on July 20 (during the March to Parliament). It was really bad. Wasn't it enough, now that the students are still being troubled? In many states, police are visiting the houses of students and threatening them with arrests," he told reporters at the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar airport.

Mr. Dipke also sought strict legal action against officials who authorised the use of pellet guns against student demonstrators at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar and warned that the government should not presume that students' anger has decreased after Mr. Pradhan's resignation.

"Whether it be Amit Shah (or anyone else), action should be taken against the person who gave orders to fire pellet guns," Mr. Dipke said.

He also warned that if need be, the students may launch a fresh agitation on a "much bigger scale".

"These students are not terrorists. They are the future of our country. If the future of the country is troubled in such a way, just as Dharmendra Pradhan had to step down...Tomorrow, we will go and change the government if it doesn't fall in line," the CJP founder added.

Arriving in his hometown, he said he was looking forward to meeting his parents. ''I am coming home after almost 40 days. Since I arrived in India, protests were going on. Then I was at Jantar Mantar in Delhi for almost 36 days. The agitation turned out to be successful and the country's students won...I have come here and I am happy that I am going to meet my parents," Mr. Dipke said.

Replying to a question, he said Prime Minister Narendra Modi should resign and become a social media influencer, "something he is very good at".

The CJP leader visited the statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar near Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University to pay respects to the chief architect of the Constitution before heading to his house in Waluj MIDC area.

Talking to reporters at his home later, he questioned the use of pellet guns against the protesters in Delhi.

''What was the reason for using pellet guns? Pellet guns should not be used against anyone. They (students) are citizens of our country and not terrorists. Whether it be (Union Home Minister) Amit Shah, action should be taken against the person who gave orders to fire pellet guns," Mr. Dipke said.

Asked about the celebration by CJP volunteers following Mr. Pradhan's resignation, which was criticised in some quarters, Mr. Dipke said there was nothing wrong with it.

''The volunteers were sitting in the harsh sun and in the rain for thirty-six days. What is wrong (with celebrating) after such a big victory. What does the BJP do after winning elections? The volunteers did not block roads like the BJP people do,'' he said.

''Did the BJP not feel any shame in felicitating Dharmendra Pradhan in Parliament after students had committed suicide,'' Mr. Dipke further asked.

When asked whether the CJP would launch another agitation, Mr. Dipke said the government was forcing it to do so.

"The government is forcing us to start a protest against....it should stop troubling the students. The anger is still there among students, because their anger was not against just one minister, but against the entire government. The government should fall in line, else the students will do it," he said.

The agitation achieved a huge victory as the youth showed that they would not be afraid of questioning the government, Mr. Dipke said.

Criticizing The Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill-2026, he said there are many laws in the country but nothing can happen until those who implement them are good people.

"Three days ago, Prime Minister Narendra Modi promised fast-track courts for paper leak cases. People were also happy. But what happened? The very first hearing of the case was postponed because the CBI counsel did not appear," he said.

title: Mollywood hails Centre’s crackdown on movie piracy network
author: G. Krishnakumar
content_html:
The Centre’s crackdown on websites and Telegram channels allegedly hosting or distributing copyright-infringing content has given a major push to the anti-piracy campaign by the Malayalam film industry.

The action against digital piracy received a shot in the arm after the Union government blocked around 1, 263 websites and over 4, 900 Telegram channels for facilitating copyright-infringing content that included pirated copies of films. The action taken was conveyed by Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to Suresh Gopi, actor and MP in a letter dated July 22, 2026.

Mr. Gopi, who had held several rounds of discussions with the representatives of the South Indian Film Producers’ Association (SIFPA) on the issue, had sought the intervention of the Centre in acting tough against the violators. The latest action was initiated under the provisions of the Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023.

The Minister’s reply stated that the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has acted on complaints by intermediaries to disable about 7, 397 URLs, including 1, 263 websites and 4, 996 Telegram channels that were allegedly involved in hosting or distributing infringing content.

Mr. Gopi said that there will be no compromise on the crackdown against digital piracy as it remains a major challenge facing the Indian film industry. He said that the producers have to be provided with all support against movie piracy as the industry depended on the investments made by them for its survival.

Major relief, says G. Suresh Kumar

G. Suresh Kumar, senior producer who had attended the meetings of SIFPA as a representative of the Kerala Film Producers’ Association (KFPA), termed the Centre’s crackdown on digital piracy as “a major relief” for the industry.

“With the authorities blocking hundreds of websites and Telegram channels, we hope that the illegal duplication and distribution of movies will come down considerably. The after-effects of the Centre’s action seem to be emerging, as it would have helped in preventing distribution of pirated versions of the movie I, Nobody that reached cinemas in the second week of July”, he said.

As per the estimates by KFPA, the Malayalam film industry had incurred losses running to crores owing to digital piracy over the last several years. “On an average, a movie having a potential to garner a profit of around 10 crore would suffer nearly ₹2 crore on account of piracy,” said M. Renjith, senior producer and former president of KFPA.

He recalled an incident in which the visuals of a suspected pirated version of the super-hit Malayalam movie Thudarum, bankrolled by his production house was played on a tourist bus operating services in Kerala on May 5, 2025.

Mr. Renjith, who filed a complaint before the cyber wing of the Kerala Police, said that the preliminary probe revealed that a person on the bus had the pirated version and it was played on the screen installed in the vehicle. There were over 20 persons travelling on the bus. “People were happily watching the pirated version of the movie without thinking about its legal consequences,” he said.

B. Rakesh, president of KFPA, said that the producers of the movie I, Nobody had secured a ‘John Doe’ (’Ashok Kumar’) order [ex parte injunctions ordered against unknown persons] from the Madras High Court ahead of its release.

title: 15 kg gold, ₹28.5 crore cash recovered from former govt bus driver in Bengal’s Birbhum
author: Shrabana Chatterjee
content_html:
The West Bengal Police officials on Wednesday (July 29) recovered 15kg gold and ₹28.5 crore cash from a former government bus driver in the Birbhum area. The accused bus driver Minar Mondal is the brother-in-law of Tulu Mondal, allegedly a close aide of Trinamool Congress leader and strongman of the Birbhum district Anubrata Mondal.

“Minar Mondal has been arrested after the raid. It was his property where this cash and gold was found. A case has been registered and investigation is ongoing,” a top police official told The Hindu on Thursday (July 30, 2026).

This cash and gold seizure has been one of the biggest in the State after such massive recoveries were made from properties linked to former Trinamool era Education Minister Partha Chatterjee’s and his aide Arpita Mukherjee. The amount recovered from Ms Mukherjee was ₹50 crore in cash and over 5 kilograms of gold. 

The cash was packed in around 35 sacks, and the gold was found as solid gold biscuits inside a humble house of Mr Minar Mondal. The police have brought in five machines to count the recovered cash and around five trunks to store them. 

The total cash recovery was around ₹28.5 crores, according to police officials. It was almost a 15-hour long operation. The gold bars recovered were valued at approximately ₹21.5 crore at current market prices. 

Mr Tulu Mondal alias Mohd Nazibuddin is an absconding businessman and influential stone trader and had close interest in the stone quarrying business in the Birbhum district. 

This comes amid a crackdown on illegal mining and sand smuggling in the Birbhum district.  

The police got a secret tip off and raided the house of Mr Minar Mondal late on Tuesday (July 28) and the cash recovery continued till Wednesday (July 29). 

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that this was a crackdown on the sand mafia and appreciated the local police for the massive cash and gold recovery. 

“West Bengal Govt’s ongoing drive against the corrupt will go on with ‘Zero Tolerance Policy against Corruption’ as our guiding principle. Let it be unequivocally clear: no person with a chequered past who has amassed wealth through the exploitation of public resources and hobnobbing with the then ruling political party will be spared. Public wealth belongs to the people, and those who loot it will face the full might of the law,” Mr Adhikari wrote on his social media on Wednesday morning. He also added that the crackdown on mafia syndicates will continue. 

Earlier in July, Mr Adhikari had accused that most of the money from stone industrial areas was siphoned off by the previous Trinamool government leading to low revenues. He also said that within one month, their new government was able to stop that revenue leakage and improve the earnings of the government. 

Interestingly, Mr Anubrata Mondal himself was previously arrested in 2022 by the Central Bureau of Investigation in the cattle smuggling scam. He spent over 25 months in prison after a disproportionate amount of cash was recovered from his properties and was later released on bail in 2024. 

In the cattle scam, the CBI and Enforcement Directorate officials are investigating 70 properties linked to Mr. Anubrata Mondal, multiple land deals, two rice mills, and other businesses.
